representativeService.normalization: each target's kernel price is divided by that target's scalar integer-add service cost
representativeService.rule: an equal-weight median within each ISA family, then an equal-weight median of the family results, rounded upward
representativeService.evenSizedMedian: the exact arithmetic mean of the middle two values
representativeService.cohort: every target listed under targets; the cohort and this rule are what a revision of either changes
representativeService.scope: these are semantic service prices for an abstract machine, not an elapsed-time prediction and not an upper bound on every sampled physical processor

instructionService.method: llvm-mca --instruction-info over the instruction forms of the Native AOT reference lowering, per pinned evidence target; an instruction form the target's scheduling model does not serve is unresolved evidence, never zero and never one
instructionService.excludedWork: a continuation that ends in a managed throw is excluded: the reference kernels refuse by returning, and the throw's own object construction, stack walk and unwind are unmodeled rather than silently zero

loopBounds.contract: the restoring-division loop runs fractionBitCount times, and the preceding width guard refuses whenever BitLength(integer) + fractionBitCount exceeds 127
the software fallback clears one set bit of the mask per iteration, so a 64-bit mask admits at most 64

one pass over the divisor's limbs, of which a 128-bit value has at most four

loopBounds.contract: both operands are odd 63-bit magnitudes when the loop is entered; each pass replaces the larger with their halved difference and leaves the smaller, so the two bit lengths' sum, at most 126, falls by at least one per pass
after pass i the running value is C(n, i) with i at most n/2, which is at least 2^i, and the checked narrowing refuses once it passes 2^64, so i never reaches 64
a bisection over a 32-bit interval, which halves on every pass
one pass per subset position above the requested one, and the subset arms admit a universe, and so a subset, of at most 64
one pass per element of a subset of a universe of at most 64
one pass per element of a subset of a universe of at most 64
the descent lowers its upper ordinal once per inner pass and once per selected element, from a universe of at most 64, so no block of the nest runs more than 128 times

kernels.inputDomainBound: every ExpressionOp the function entry admits, over the argument domain each arm validates before it computes: the whole 64-bit raw carrier for the integer-factor arms, 32-bit sizes for choose and factorial, and a universe of at most 64 for the subset arms
